item.title: Lionel Messi’s international retirement serves as a reminder: Watch him while you still can
item.description:
The Argentine’s career with Argentina was singular, and his exit is a reminder that all good things come to an end It was among the defining moments of the 2026 World Cup: Lionel Messi standing arms akimbo, looking up towards Argentina’s fervent supporters after losing the final . Tears streamed down his face after his team’s embarrassing loss to Spain in what we now know was Messi’s final match wearing that famous Argentina kit. It was not the first time he’d cried at the tournament. There had been tears of joy in Argentina’s opening match, when Messi rolled back the clock to his glory days with a trio of spectacular goals against Algeria. There had been more when his brace against Austria pushed Argentina through to the knockout round as group winners, and even more when his equalizer against Egypt threw la Albiceleste a much-needed lifeline. item.title: This principal in Nepal evacuated 900 students before flooding swept away their school
item.description:
Roughly 160 people are dead and hundreds more — including dozens of international tourists — are missing after flash floods hit a region on the mountainous border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday. Devastating footage posted to social media shows people fleeing a wall of water that washed away buildings and vehicles. Initial analysis of satellite imagery and reports from the Nepalese government indicate that the flooding was likely triggered by a landslide caused after a piece of a glacier fell hundreds of feet. As the region warms, its ice is becoming increasingly unstable , raising the risk of catastrophic flooding. “The glaciers over there are definitely in retreat,” said Joseph Shea, an associate professor of geography at the University of Northern British Columbia. “There’s a lot of glacier mass up there, but we’re seeing thinning, we’re seeing retreating.” Since 2000, the world’s…

item.title: Canada erects giant ‘Lake Ontario’ sign as spat with Trump over name escalates
item.description:
Photo Illustration by Eric Faison/The Daily Beast/Getty Images/Reuters Donald Trump flew into a Truth Social meltdown after a top Canadian politician delivered a withering Saturday Night Live diss. Just before 10 a.m. on Sunday, after a bizarre goose-themed AI slop spiral , the 80-year-old president was already in meltdown mode over his trade war with America’s northern neighbor. “Canadian businesses are pouring into the United States. We want to make our own cars, etc. That’s what’s going to happen. Canada has been ripping us off for years — NO LONGER!” he said. At the same time, Ontario Premier Doug Ford appeared on ABC’s This Week to slam Trump and delivered a line that is sure to have riled the notoriously thin-skinned president. Read more at The Daily Beast.

item.title: Nepal disaster: fake and AI images flood social media as deaths mount
item.description:
Total of 804 confirmed dead and more than 3,000 missing amid threat of fresh inundation ‘Their whole village has disappeared’: frantic hunt for survivors in Kathmandu hospital Rescuers in Nepal and Tibet have battled through leg-sucking mud amid the threat of fresh flooding to search for thousands of people still missing after a deadly wall of water swept through the Himalayan border zone, engulfing entire villages. The latest updates on Sunday put the number of missing at 3,048, including hundreds of foreigners. There was a total of 804 confirmed deaths across Nepal and Tibet, and reports of some bodies swept downstream possibly as far as India. Continue reading...

item.title: Nepal rescuers blast hillside in search of hydropower workers as families wait anxiously
item.description:
Workers thought to be stuck in underground areas at 11 sites after last week’s devastating flash floods Rescue teams are working to reach more than 900 missing hydropower workers, hundreds of whom are feared trapped in the tunnels and underground areas of 12 hydropower projects in Nepal after the devastating flash floods , the ⁠country’s disaster management authority has said. The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud and debris on Wednesday last week has risen to 939 people, with 16 more dead reported in Tibet. More than 4,400 are missing on the two sides of the border. Continue reading...
